correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite length-two chain rings, square-zero lifts of canonical reduction J satisfy NY+YN=0. The displayed conjugation I+pi C eliminates all free blocks except the canonical homology block, while the residue centralizer acts on it exactly by similarity. A converse lifted block-diagonal conjugator proves classification. Rational-canonical form gives the class generating function; independent group-orbit exhaustive computation matched all enumerated n<=3, q=2 and n<=2, q=3 in both split and mixed-characteristic rings.

originality.rationale: Inspected general extension theory, square-zero matrix similarity over domains, and two close labeled Bockstein/Smith censuses do not compute the full GL_n(R) conjugacy quotient of the square-zero locus for all n. The present identification of four explicit gauge directions and residual ordinary similarity is not an implication of mere counting by ranks or normal-form existence. General extension-orbit methods provide the prior framework, and unindexed equivalent treatments remain a real priority risk.
residual_risks: The general extension-orbit method of Prasad–Singla–Spallone may permit an equivalent special-case classification in uninspected sections or secondary literature; no exhaustive priority determination is asserted.
A specialized theorem in older square-zero representations over truncated discrete valuation rings might present the same canonical forms under module-isomorphism language.

Earlier general dual-number similarity literature, including Trishin (2009), may contain special constrained classifications not indexed by their abstracts or introductions; only its introductory material was inspected.

value.rationale: Classifies every isomorphism type of a square-zero differential on free modules over every finite length-two chain ring in any dimension. It refines coarser labeled Smith/Bockstein rank strata by the full rational canonical type of the reduced homology endomorphism and produces a uniform all-dimension orbit generating function. This is a natural complete classification with structural use for differential modules over short local rings, not an arbitrary finite example.
